question: Find the shortest distance between the lines $\vec{r}=\hat{i}+\lambda(\hat{i}+\hat{j})$ and $\vec{r}=\hat{j}+\hat{k}+\mu(\hat{i}-\hat{j})$.
explanation:
Step 1: Position and direction vectors
Write the lines as $\vec{r}=\vec{a}_1+\lambda\vec{b}_1$ and $\vec{r}=\vec{a}_2+\mu\vec{b}_2$, where
$$\vec{a}_1=\hat{i},\quad \vec{b}_1=\hat{i}+\hat{j},\quad \vec{a}_2=\hat{j}+\hat{k},\quad \vec{b}_2=\hat{i}-\hat{j}.$$
Step 2: Vector joining points on the lines
$$\vec{a}_2-\vec{a}_1=-\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}.$$
Step 3: Common perpendicular direction
$$\vec{b}_1\times\vec{b}_2=(\hat{i}+\hat{j})\times(\hat{i}-\hat{j})=-2\hat{k},$$
so $|\vec{b}_1\times\vec{b}_2|=2$.
Step 4: Shortest-distance formula
$$d=\frac{|(\vec{a}_2-\vec{a}_1)\cdot(\vec{b}_1\times\vec{b}_2)|}{|\vec{b}_1\times\vec{b}_2|}.$$
Hence,
$$d=\frac{|(-\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})\cdot(-2\hat{k})|}{2}=\frac{2}{2}=1.$$
Step 5: Final result
Therefore, the shortest distance between the two lines is $1$ unit.
